start.title: Getting started
start.summary: A project is a folder on your disk: people, events, media and backups live there. There is no server and no account.
start.step1: On the Projects screen, create a project or open an existing folder.
start.step2: Import data from AT5 or GEDCOM: the import creates a new project and never changes the source file.
start.step3: Keep the project folder in your own backup: the app keeps internal copies, but an external copy is safer.
start.note: One app instance writes to a project at a time. Do not open the same folder in two copies of the app.

people.title: People
people.summary: A person card keeps names, gender, life dates, a photo, events and relationships.
people.step1: On the People screen, press Add and fill in the name.
people.step2: Open a person in the side panel to see facts, events, media and relationships.
people.step3: Use Edit to change the card. Deleting a person keeps events that have other participants.
people.note: A person can have several names; the primary one is shown in lists and in the tree.

relations.title: Relationships
relations.summary: Relationships are explicit: parent and child, spouse, partner and adoption. Siblings are derived from shared parents.
relations.step1: Open the relationships section of a person card.
relations.step2: Add a parent, a child, a spouse or a partner and choose the other person from the list.
relations.step3: Use the separate adoption type when a parent is adoptive.
relations.note: The app stores no sibling links and rejects duplicates, self-links and cycles.

events.title: Events
events.summary: An event has a type, a date, a place, participants and optional detail fields.
events.step1: On the Events screen, press Add and choose the type.
events.step2: Enter the date. If only the year or the month is known, choose that precision instead of a full date.
events.step3: Add the place and participants, then fill in the detail fields of the chosen type.
events.note: Unknown dates are never replaced by invented ones: the original value is kept with unknown precision.

tree.title: Tree and kinship
tree.summary: The tree is built from one person: ancestors, descendants or the whole tree.
tree.step1: On the Tree screen, choose the person who becomes the root.
tree.step2: Switch the layout and the zoom level.
tree.step3: To connect two people, open Relation: the app shows the path and the kinship terms.
tree.note: Kinship labels are calculated from the person you selected.

find.title: Search and checks
find.summary: Full-text search covers people and events, the timeline shows dated events, and data checks find problems.
find.step1: Type a query in Search and open a person or an event from the results.
find.step2: On the Timeline, filter events by type, person and period.
find.step3: Run the project check on the Projects page and review every warning.
find.note: A check never changes data; it only points at what is worth fixing.

data.title: Import, export and media
data.summary: AT5 and GEDCOM import creates a project; export writes GEDCOM or a JSON/ZIP archive. Media is stored in the project folder with a checksum.
data.step1: Import a file on the Import screen: a report is shown first and writing starts only after you confirm.
data.step2: Export the project to GEDCOM or JSON/ZIP from the project menu.
data.step3: Attach photos and files in a person card; the file is copied into the project.
data.note: Importing the same file again does not create duplicates and does not overwrite manual edits.

assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.summary: The chat answers questions about your archive and about the app, using built-in read-only tools.
assistant.step1: Enable chat in Settings and set an OpenAI-compatible base URL, a model and the name of the environment variable that holds the key.
assistant.step2: Ask in Chat; people and events found in the archive open by link.
assistant.step3: Proposed person edits are shown for review and applied only after you confirm.
assistant.note: Nothing is sent until a provider is configured. The key stays in an environment variable, not in the project.
